to_numpy(*self*,*zero_copy_only=True*,*writable=False*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.FixedSizeBinaryArray.to_numpy)
- Return a NumPy view or copy of this array. - By default, tries to return a view of this array. This is only supported for primitive arrays with the same memory layout as NumPy (i.e. integers, floating point, ..) and without any nulls. - For the extension arrays, this method simply delegates to the underlying storage array. - Parameters:
- **zero_copy_only**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- If True, an exception will be raised if the conversion to a numpy array would require copying the underlying data (e.g. in presence of nulls, or for non-primitive types).
- **writable**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- For numpy arrays created with zero copy (view on the Arrow data), the resulting array is not writable (Arrow data is immutable). By setting this to True, a copy of the array is made to ensure it is writable.

- Returns:
- **array**- `numpy.ndarray`

to_pandas(*self*,*memory_pool=None*,*categories=None*,*bool strings_to_categorical=False*,*bool zero_copy_only=False*,*bool integer_object_nulls=False*,*bool date_as_object=True*,*bool timestamp_as_object=False*,*bool use_threads=True*,*bool deduplicate_objects=True*,*bool ignore_metadata=False*,*bool safe=True*,*bool split_blocks=False*,*bool self_destruct=False*,*str maps_as_pydicts=None*,*types_mapper=None*,*bool coerce_temporal_nanoseconds=False*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.FixedSizeBinaryArray.to_pandas)
- Convert to a pandas-compatible NumPy array or DataFrame, as appropriate - Parameters:
- **memory_pool**- `MemoryPool`- `None`
- Arrow MemoryPool to use for allocations. Uses the default memory pool if not passed.
- **categories**- `list`- `empty`
- List of fields that should be returned as pandas.Categorical. Only applies to table-like data structures.
- **strings_to_categorical**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Encode string (UTF8) and binary types to pandas.Categorical.
- **zero_copy_only**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Raise an ArrowException if this function call would require copying the underlying data.
- **integer_object_nulls**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Cast integers with nulls to objects
- **date_as_object**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Cast dates to objects. If False, convert to datetime64 dtype with the equivalent time unit (if supported). Note: in pandas version < 2.0, only datetime64[ns] conversion is supported.
- **timestamp_as_object**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Cast non-nanosecond timestamps (np.datetime64) to objects. This is useful in pandas version 1.x if you have timestamps that don’t fit in the normal date range of nanosecond timestamps (1678 CE-2262 CE). Non-nanosecond timestamps are supported in pandas version 2.0. If False, all timestamps are converted to datetime64 dtype.
- **use_threads**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Whether to parallelize the conversion using multiple threads.
- **deduplicate_objects**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Do not create multiple copies Python objects when created, to save on memory use. Conversion will be slower.
- **ignore_metadata**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- If True, do not use the ‘pandas’ metadata to reconstruct the DataFrame index, if present
- **safe**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- For certain data types, a cast is needed in order to store the data in a pandas DataFrame or Series (e.g. timestamps are always stored as nanoseconds in pandas). This option controls whether it is a safe cast or not.
- **split_blocks**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- If True, generate one internal “block” for each column when creating a pandas.DataFrame from a RecordBatch or Table. While this can temporarily reduce memory note that various pandas operations can trigger “consolidation” which may balloon memory use.
- **self_destruct**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- EXPERIMENTAL: If True, attempt to deallocate the originating Arrow memory while converting the Arrow object to pandas. If you use the object after calling to_pandas with this option it will crash your program. - Note that you may not see always memory usage improvements. For example, if multiple columns share an underlying allocation, memory can’t be freed until all columns are converted.
- **maps_as_pydicts**- `str`
- Valid values are None, ‘lossy’, or ‘strict’. The default behavior (None), is to convert Arrow Map arrays to Python association lists (list-of-tuples) in the same order as the Arrow Map, as in [(key1, value1), (key2, value2), …]. - If ‘lossy’ or ‘strict’, convert Arrow Map arrays to native Python dicts. This can change the ordering of (key, value) pairs, and will deduplicate multiple keys, resulting in a possible loss of data. - If ‘lossy’, this key deduplication results in a warning printed when detected. If ‘strict’, this instead results in an exception being raised when detected.
- **types_mapper**function, default- `None`
- A function mapping a pyarrow DataType to a pandas ExtensionDtype. This can be used to override the default pandas type for conversion of built-in pyarrow types or in absence of pandas_metadata in the Table schema. The function receives a pyarrow DataType and is expected to return a pandas ExtensionDtype or - `None`if the default conversion should be used for that type. If you have a dictionary mapping, you can pass- `dict.get`as function.
- **coerce_temporal_nanoseconds**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Only applicable to pandas version >= 2.0. A legacy option to coerce date32, date64, duration, and timestamp time units to nanoseconds when converting to pandas. This is the default behavior in pandas version 1.x. Set this option to True if you’d like to use this coercion when using pandas version >= 2.0 for backwards compatibility (not recommended otherwise).

- Returns:
- `pandas.Series`- `pandas.DataFrame`- `type`

 - Examples - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> import pandas as pd - Convert a Table to pandas DataFrame: - >>> table = pa.table([ ... pa.array([2, 4, 5, 100]), ... pa.array(["Flamingo", "Horse", "Brittle stars", "Centipede"]) ... ], names=['n_legs', 'animals']) >>> table.to_pandas() n_legs animals 0 2 Flamingo 1 4 Horse 2 5 Brittle stars 3 100 Centipede >>> isinstance(table.to_pandas(), pd.DataFrame) True - Convert a RecordBatch to pandas DataFrame: - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> n_legs = pa.array([2, 4, 5, 100]) >>> animals = pa.array(["Flamingo", "Horse", "Brittle stars", "Centipede"]) >>> batch = pa.record_batch([n_legs, animals], ... names=["n_legs", "animals"]) >>> batch pyarrow.RecordBatch n_legs: int64 animals: string ---- n_legs: [2,4,5,100] animals: ["Flamingo","Horse","Brittle stars","Centipede"] >>> batch.to_pandas() n_legs animals 0 2 Flamingo 1 4 Horse 2 5 Brittle stars 3 100 Centipede >>> isinstance(batch.to_pandas(), pd.DataFrame) True - Convert a Chunked Array to pandas Series: - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> n_legs = pa.chunked_array([[2, 2, 4], [4, 5, 100]]) >>> n_legs.to_pandas() 0 2 1 2 2 4 3 4 4 5 5 100 dtype: int64 >>> isinstance(n_legs.to_pandas(), pd.Series) True

to_numpy(*self*,*zero_copy_only=True*,*writable=False*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.FixedSizeListArray.to_numpy)
- Return a NumPy view or copy of this array. - By default, tries to return a view of this array. This is only supported for primitive arrays with the same memory layout as NumPy (i.e. integers, floating point, ..) and without any nulls. - For the extension arrays, this method simply delegates to the underlying storage array. - Parameters:
- **zero_copy_only**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- If True, an exception will be raised if the conversion to a numpy array would require copying the underlying data (e.g. in presence of nulls, or for non-primitive types).
- **writable**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- For numpy arrays created with zero copy (view on the Arrow data), the resulting array is not writable (Arrow data is immutable). By setting this to True, a copy of the array is made to ensure it is writable.

- Returns:
- **array**- `numpy.ndarray`

to_pandas(*self*,*memory_pool=None*,*categories=None*,*bool strings_to_categorical=False*,*bool zero_copy_only=False*,*bool integer_object_nulls=False*,*bool date_as_object=True*,*bool timestamp_as_object=False*,*bool use_threads=True*,*bool deduplicate_objects=True*,*bool ignore_metadata=False*,*bool safe=True*,*bool split_blocks=False*,*bool self_destruct=False*,*str maps_as_pydicts=None*,*types_mapper=None*,*bool coerce_temporal_nanoseconds=False*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.FixedSizeListArray.to_pandas)
- Convert to a pandas-compatible NumPy array or DataFrame, as appropriate - Parameters:
- **memory_pool**- `MemoryPool`- `None`
- Arrow MemoryPool to use for allocations. Uses the default memory pool if not passed.
- **categories**- `list`- `empty`
- List of fields that should be returned as pandas.Categorical. Only applies to table-like data structures.
- **strings_to_categorical**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Encode string (UTF8) and binary types to pandas.Categorical.
- **zero_copy_only**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Raise an ArrowException if this function call would require copying the underlying data.
- **integer_object_nulls**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Cast integers with nulls to objects
- **date_as_object**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Cast dates to objects. If False, convert to datetime64 dtype with the equivalent time unit (if supported). Note: in pandas version < 2.0, only datetime64[ns] conversion is supported.
- **timestamp_as_object**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Cast non-nanosecond timestamps (np.datetime64) to objects. This is useful in pandas version 1.x if you have timestamps that don’t fit in the normal date range of nanosecond timestamps (1678 CE-2262 CE). Non-nanosecond timestamps are supported in pandas version 2.0. If False, all timestamps are converted to datetime64 dtype.
- **use_threads**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Whether to parallelize the conversion using multiple threads.
- **deduplicate_objects**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- Do not create multiple copies Python objects when created, to save on memory use. Conversion will be slower.
- **ignore_metadata**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- If True, do not use the ‘pandas’ metadata to reconstruct the DataFrame index, if present
- **safe**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `True`
- For certain data types, a cast is needed in order to store the data in a pandas DataFrame or Series (e.g. timestamps are always stored as nanoseconds in pandas). This option controls whether it is a safe cast or not.
- **split_blocks**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- If True, generate one internal “block” for each column when creating a pandas.DataFrame from a RecordBatch or Table. While this can temporarily reduce memory note that various pandas operations can trigger “consolidation” which may balloon memory use.
- **self_destruct**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- EXPERIMENTAL: If True, attempt to deallocate the originating Arrow memory while converting the Arrow object to pandas. If you use the object after calling to_pandas with this option it will crash your program. - Note that you may not see always memory usage improvements. For example, if multiple columns share an underlying allocation, memory can’t be freed until all columns are converted.
- **maps_as_pydicts**- `str`
- Valid values are None, ‘lossy’, or ‘strict’. The default behavior (None), is to convert Arrow Map arrays to Python association lists (list-of-tuples) in the same order as the Arrow Map, as in [(key1, value1), (key2, value2), …]. - If ‘lossy’ or ‘strict’, convert Arrow Map arrays to native Python dicts. This can change the ordering of (key, value) pairs, and will deduplicate multiple keys, resulting in a possible loss of data. - If ‘lossy’, this key deduplication results in a warning printed when detected. If ‘strict’, this instead results in an exception being raised when detected.
- **types_mapper**function, default- `None`
- A function mapping a pyarrow DataType to a pandas ExtensionDtype. This can be used to override the default pandas type for conversion of built-in pyarrow types or in absence of pandas_metadata in the Table schema. The function receives a pyarrow DataType and is expected to return a pandas ExtensionDtype or - `None`if the default conversion should be used for that type. If you have a dictionary mapping, you can pass- `dict.get`as function.
- **coerce_temporal_nanoseconds**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values), default- `False`
- Only applicable to pandas version >= 2.0. A legacy option to coerce date32, date64, duration, and timestamp time units to nanoseconds when converting to pandas. This is the default behavior in pandas version 1.x. Set this option to True if you’d like to use this coercion when using pandas version >= 2.0 for backwards compatibility (not recommended otherwise).

- Returns:
- `pandas.Series`- `pandas.DataFrame`- `type`

 - Examples - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> import pandas as pd - Convert a Table to pandas DataFrame: - >>> table = pa.table([ ... pa.array([2, 4, 5, 100]), ... pa.array(["Flamingo", "Horse", "Brittle stars", "Centipede"]) ... ], names=['n_legs', 'animals']) >>> table.to_pandas() n_legs animals 0 2 Flamingo 1 4 Horse 2 5 Brittle stars 3 100 Centipede >>> isinstance(table.to_pandas(), pd.DataFrame) True - Convert a RecordBatch to pandas DataFrame: - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> n_legs = pa.array([2, 4, 5, 100]) >>> animals = pa.array(["Flamingo", "Horse", "Brittle stars", "Centipede"]) >>> batch = pa.record_batch([n_legs, animals], ... names=["n_legs", "animals"]) >>> batch pyarrow.RecordBatch n_legs: int64 animals: string ---- n_legs: [2,4,5,100] animals: ["Flamingo","Horse","Brittle stars","Centipede"] >>> batch.to_pandas() n_legs animals 0 2 Flamingo 1 4 Horse 2 5 Brittle stars 3 100 Centipede >>> isinstance(batch.to_pandas(), pd.DataFrame) True - Convert a Chunked Array to pandas Series: - >>> import pyarrow as pa >>> n_legs = pa.chunked_array([[2, 2, 4], [4, 5, 100]]) >>> n_legs.to_pandas() 0 2 1 2 2 4 3 4 4 5 5 100 dtype: int64 >>> isinstance(n_legs.to_pandas(), pd.Series) True

# pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow-flight-clientmiddleware)

class pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware)
- Bases: - `_Weakrefable`- Client-side middleware for a call, instantiated per RPC. - Methods here should be fast and must be infallible: they should not raise exceptions or stall indefinitely. -
__init__(**args*,***kwargs*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware.__init__)
 - Methods - `__init__`- `call_completed`- A callback when the call finishes. - `received_headers`- A callback when headers are received. - `sending_headers`- A callback before headers are sent. -
call_completed(*self*,*exception*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware.call_completed)
- A callback when the call finishes. - The default implementation does nothing. - Parameters:
- **exception**- `ArrowException`
- If the call errored, this is the equivalent exception. Will be None if the call succeeded.

received_headers(*self*,*headers*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware.received_headers)
- A callback when headers are received. - The default implementation does nothing. - Parameters:
- **headers**- `dict`
- A dictionary of headers from the server. Keys are strings and values are lists of strings (for text headers) or bytes (for binary headers).

sending_headers(*self*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.ClientMiddleware.sending_headers)
- A callback before headers are sent. - Returns:
- **headers**- `dict`
- A dictionary of header values to add to the request, or None if no headers are to be added. The dictionary should have string keys and string or list-of-string values. - Bytes values are allowed, but the underlying transport may not support them or may restrict them. For gRPC, binary values are only allowed on headers ending in “-bin”. - Header names must be lowercase ASCII.

# pyarrow.flight.FlightClient[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow-flight-flightclient)

class pyarrow.flight.FlightClient(*location*,*tls_root_certs=None*,***,*cert_chain=None*,*private_key=None*,*override_hostname=None*,*middleware=None*,*write_size_limit_bytes=None*,*disable_server_verification=None*,*generic_options=None*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.FlightClient)
- Bases: - `_Weakrefable`- A client to a Flight service. - Connect to a Flight service on the given host and port. - Parameters:
- **location**- `str`- `tuple`- `Location`
- Location to connect to. Either a gRPC URI like grpc://localhost:port, a tuple of (host, port) pair, or a Location instance.
- **tls_root_certs**- `bytes`- `None`
- PEM-encoded
- **cert_chain: bytes or None**
- Client certificate if using mutual TLS
- **private_key: bytes or None**
- Client private key for cert_chain is using mutual TLS
- **override_hostname**- `str`- `None`
- Override the hostname checked by TLS. Insecure, use with caution.
- **middleware**- `list`- `None`
- A list of ClientMiddlewareFactory instances.
- **write_size_limit_bytes**- `int`- `None`
- A soft limit on the size of a data payload sent to the server. Enabled if positive. If enabled, writing a record batch that (when serialized) exceeds this limit will raise an exception; the client can retry the write with a smaller batch.
- **disable_server_verification**- [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bltin-boolean-values)optional, default- `False`
- A flag that indicates that, if the client is connecting with TLS, that it skips server verification. If this is enabled, all other TLS settings are overridden.
- **generic_options**- `list`- `None`
- A list of generic (string, int or string) option tuples passed to the underlying transport. Effect is implementation dependent.

# pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint &#8212; Apache Arrow v24.0.0

Source: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/generated/pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint.html

# pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow-flight-flightendpoint)

class pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint(*ticket*,*locations*,*expiration_time=None*,*app_metadata=''*)[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint)
- Bases: - `_Weakrefable`- A Flight stream, along with the ticket and locations to access it. -
__init__()[#](https://arrow.apache.org#pyarrow.flight.FlightEndpoint.__init__)
- Create a FlightEndpoint from a ticket and list of locations. - Parameters:
- **ticket**- `Ticket`- `bytes`
- the ticket needed to access this flight
- **locations**- `list`- `str`- `URIs`
- locations where this flight is available
- **expiration_time**- `TimestampScalar`, default- `None`
- Expiration time of this stream. If present, clients may assume they can retry DoGet requests. Otherwise, clients should avoid retrying DoGet requests.
- **app_metadata**- `bytes`- `str`
- Application-defined opaque metadata.

- Raises:
